scope: REQ45 / MATURE06-05 installed dictation stop vs cancel, read-only interface research

findings.fact: Installed core0.3.22 send invokes active session.cancel synchronously and cleanup, then snapshots current text. It does not await stop/final transcription. WebSpeech cancel invokes recognition.abort. Official guide generic wording automatically stopped must not be interpreted as final transcription awaited.
findings.implication: Product must explicitly define sending while recording/transcribing. Preferred user acceptance: stop/finish to editable text, then explicit Send or Queue; command authority must reject active recording/transcribing if that is the chosen policy. UI disable alone is insufficient.

findings.source: base-composer-runtime-core.ts:1151-1177; official guide custom adapter stop example
findings.fact: stopDictation calls session.stop, then cleans runtime subscriptions on Promise settlement. The documented custom MediaRecorder stop example returns without waiting for asynchronous onstop fetch/transcript.
findings.inference: Copying that example literally can settle early and detach runtime callbacks before final transcript. Adapter stop must resolve only after final delivery or terminal error/cancellation; no prematurely ended status either, because core polls status every100ms.

findings.fact: setText/reset rebase a live dictation session; base dispose handles attachment preparation, not dictation. Core guards callbacks by its dictation session ID, which does not represent Flow pane/namespace/auth/draft generations.
findings.inference: Replacing a draft or switching/revoking a Flow owner must invalidate a private voice lease and cancel the exact adapter session before replacement. Do not equate setText, attachment dispose or generic cancel with dictation cancellation. Async mic acquisition/transcription completion must recheck lease after every await before emitting or changing any status. Stop finalizes; cancellation discards pending results. Already committed/user-edited text policy must be explicit, not an accidental rollback.

findings.fact: Native stop attempts a final recognition result; abort does not. Built-in adapter waits for terminal state with a5s timeout then aborts. Support check only detects constructor presence.
findings.implication: Keep real capability/error states, a bounded stop timeout, idempotent cleanup, stream-track release, fetch AbortSignal and stale callback rejection. Constructor existence does not prove locale, permission, offline processing or recognition availability. Voice processing mode must be truthful; browser recognition is not assumed local.

acceptance: Explicit stop retains final editable text exactly once; stop promise remains pending during delayed final transcription.
Send and Queue during recording/transcribing follow the same declared policy at actual command entry, with no accidental partial transcript or automatic POST.
Cancel before getUserMedia resolves stops late tracks and emits no draft mutation; cancel during fetch aborts request and rejects late response even if abort races.
Pane switch, auth replacement, draft replacement and plugin disable invalidate old callbacks without mutating the next draft; same-pane ordinary user edits are handled deliberately.
Late end/error from sessionA cannot clean sessionB; repeated stop/cancel/dispose is harmless; typing and final-text concatenation do not duplicate transcript.
Actual capability/language/mime/microphone and complete flow remain separately unverified; mock adapter/source review cannot close Voice delivery.
limits: No mic/provider/model/service/browser/test or product imports; dependency source read only.
This is design evidence for an unimplemented feature, not a reproduced product defect or a new claim.
Official guide and installed source must be distinguished; installed source controls the exact existing stack.
No runtime or performance result inferred.
cleanCode: One existing composer adapter and private generation lease; explicit terminal state; one finalization promise; no parallel microphone UI or second command/draft authority.
